entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Notice of Compliance (NOC) Data Extracts
entries.description: The data extract is a series of compressed ASCII text files of the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database.
entries.summary: A new data extract of the Notice of Compliance (NOC) database has been released as compressed ASCII text files.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams that need to review or analyze NOC data should be aware of the availability of this extract for regulatory research or compliance monitoring.

entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Clinical trial applications advice pilot becomes permanent
entries.description: The Accelerating Clinical Trials in the EU (ACT EU) advice pilot, which helps sponsors prepare clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027…
entries.summary: The ACT EU advice pilot, which assists sponsors in preparing clinical trial applications, will become a permanent initiative from January 2027.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams will need to incorporate the permanent ACT EU guidance into their application preparation workflows and ensure compliance with the newly established procedures.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Product monograph brand safety updates
entries.description: Product monograph brand safety updates for Submissions cleared between 01-09-2026 and 30-09-2026
entries.summary: Updated brand safety information has been added to product monographs for submissions cleared between 1 September 2026 and 30 September 2026.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling these submissions need to review the revised monographs to ensure compliance with the new brand safety requirements.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to reporting and providing information on drug shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0120)
entries.description: This document is intended to help market authorization holders comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: This guide provides instructions on reporting drug shortages and discontinuations to comply with sections C.01.014.8 to C.01.014.91 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must follow the guidance to accurately report shortages and discontinuations, ensuring regulatory compliance for all products.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide to distributing drugs intended for the Canadian market for consumption or use outside Canada (GUI-0145)
entries.description: This document is intended to help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: A new guideline clarifies how drug licence holders can distribute drugs intended for the Canadian market to be consumed or used outside Canada, in line with sections C.01.014.94 to C.01.014.95 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams responsible for international distribution of Canadian‑market drugs must review this guideline to ensure compliance when exporting products for use abroad.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on the exceptional importation and sale of drugs in response to shortages and discontinuations (GUI-0148)
entries.description: This document will help drug establishment licence holders comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: Provides guidance for drug establishment licence holders on the importation and sale of drugs in response to shortages and discontinuations.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must comply with sections C.10.004 to C.10.013 of the Food and Drug Regulations, affecting all drug establishments when sourcing and supplying drugs during shortages.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Guide on extending expiration dates of marketed drugs in response to drug shortages (GUI-0500)
entries.description: This document will help market authorization holders and drug establishment licence holders understand how to comply with sections C.010.014 to C.10.021 of the Food and Drug Regulations
entries.summary: Guidance on extending expiration dates of marketed drugs to address shortages.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams for all drug holders must ensure compliance with the specified regulation sections to maintain product availability during shortages.

entries.label: Health Canada
entries.title: Register of Innovative Drugs
entries.description: A listing of drugs pursuant to sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.summary: A new register lists drugs that fall under sub-section C.08.004.1(9) of the Food and Drug Regulations.
entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory affairs teams must verify whether their products are included and ensure ongoing compliance with listing requirements.

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams involved in centralised procedure applications should review the updated guidance to ensure compliance with the latest procedural expectations.

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should be aware that the updated extract provides comprehensive data for all products, impacting data collection and reporting for submissions.

entries.title: Advice on ‘end-of-year’ submission dates for type I variations in 2026
entries.description: Marketing authorisation holders wishing to receive an outcome in 2026 should submit type IA annual updates, individual type IA and type IAIN variations, and super-groupings…
entries.summary: Regulators advise that to obtain an outcome in 2026, holders must submit type IA annual updates, individual type IA and type IAIN variations, and super-groupings by the end of the year.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams handling type I variations must ensure submissions are timely to receive outcomes in 2026.

entries.label: EMA News

entries.description: EMA has endorsed a joint statement from the International Coalition of Medicines Regulatory Authorities (ICMRA) calling on medicine developers, manufacturers, regulators and…

entries.why_it_matters: Regulatory teams should recognize that future regulatory guidance may increasingly favor non‑animal testing methods, impacting development and approval strategies.
